## [machine/torsion-box.md](machine/torsion-box.md)  (8)

- ⚠️ [L41](machine/torsion-box.md#the-box) — *The torsion box and its base / The box*<br>The grid spacing is not decided. Every tenon rises into the cavity, so no rib may cross one - but that lands differently for the front and back posts. See "What the tenons ask of the grid" below.
- 🔴 [L121](machine/torsion-box.md#if-more-stiffness-is-wanted-rib-height-beats-thicker-skins) — *The box / If more stiffness is wanted, rib height beats thi…*<br>What does deserve the material is the back edge. With posts at the front corners and the middle of the back, the back edge is a beam supported at its midpoint, carrying both back corners - and those corners cannot be propped, because the rear carcases sit right under them and letting the box land on one destroys the three-point mount. Skin thickness is a weak lever on a spanning problem; a deep back-edge member, running below the bottom skin if it has to, is the right spend.
- ⚠️ [L199](machine/torsion-box.md#ledge-depth-follows-the-wall-above-it---and-it-is-not-19-mm-everywhere) — *The three load-bearing points / Ledge depth follows the wal…*<br>48 mm is where the corner tenons stop being generous. They carry no vertical load - that is all on the shoulder - and they have 99 mm of engagement, so this is location duty only. But the rule below about cutting each hole to its own post matters more at 48 mm than it did at 67, and a 38 mm ledge on two adjacent faces of a stick that measures 88.9 rather than 86 leaves ~51 mm, not 48.
- ⚠️ [L220](machine/torsion-box.md#bearing-and-the-shoulder-that-stopped-being-single-sided) — *The three load-bearing points / Bearing, and the shoulder t…*<br>Cut each hole to its own post. 86 mm is the working figure; S4S 4×4 is commonly 88.9 mm, and cedar varies between sticks. - 🔴 [L303](machine/torsion-box.md#the-shear-walls) — *The base / The shear walls*<br>Edge fastening is what makes a shear wall a shear wall. A panel transfers load only through its perimeter connections: glue plus screws at roughly 150 mm all the way round - to the bottom frame, the top frame, the posts, and carcase-to-carcase where they meet. A carcase that merely sits in the void with screws in its corners contributes close to nothing, and looks identical to one that works.
- ⚠️ [L309](machine/torsion-box.md#the-shear-walls) — *The base / The shear walls*<br>The left and right sides are the least-stiffened perimeter. The rear carcases cover the back and the front carcase covers the front; the sides get only carcase ends. That is where to add a panel if more is ever wanted - and it is also the least useful face for storage access, so it may be free.
- ⚠️ [L349](machine/torsion-box.md#drain-ports---and-why-they-cannot-go-in-the-bottom-skin) — *Transport / Drain ports - and why they cannot go in the bot…*<br>Keep them out of the laminated left and right walls. Those are the 38 mm shear webs the Y beam plates bolt to; a 2 inch hole through one is a hole in the load path.
- 🔴 [L351](machine/torsion-box.md#drain-ports---and-why-they-cannot-go-in-the-bottom-skin) — *Transport / Drain ports - and why they cannot go in the bot…*<br>A rib grid makes closed cells, and each cell traps its own sand. Either a port per cell, or notch the ribs at the bottom so sand can migrate to a few ports. The notches cost a little glue line to the bottom skin and nothing else.

If indicator 4 stays at a fixed spot while the blocks move away from it, the (3−4) difference quietly starts including carriage-plate bending and stops meaning "the Z assembly". Put it beside wherever the blocks are for that run.

It is not a modal analysis.
